extractions.value: Authors propose the term 'Stiff Hemisyndrome' as a junction between SLS and SPS; possible link between SLS and previous cervical myelopathy suggested; initial misdiagnosis of primary anxiety disorder with psychogenic dystonia; ENMG performed under bromazepam and baclofen was normal.
extractions.quote: We report a case of right-sided SLS, which could be defined as 'Stiff Hemisyndrome', as a junction between SLS and SPS. Interestingly, in this case, a link between SLS and previous cervical myelopathy can be suspected. This presentation first led to the erroneous diagnosis of a primary anxiety disorder with psychogenic dystonia. Electroneuromyography (ENMG) carried out under bromazepam and baclofen was normal.
